phase3_12_config.pipeline: question -> extract_item_reference() (new, this task, text-only regex over the same canonical Item-id set Task 2.8 already detects) + Task 3.8-style (cik, fiscal_year) text extraction -> resolve_filing_document_id() against the frozen `submissions` table (data/xbrl.duckdb, form='10-K') -> load_document_nodes() for that ONE document only -> filter to section_id == requested item -> return only those nodes. No retrieval, no embedding call, no generation, no full-corpus scan anywhere in this path.
phase3_12_config.scope_decision: PROJECT_EXECUTION.md's Task 3.12 example ('Summarize Item 7 of this filing') has ZERO matching examples anywhere in the 1,932-question DEV corpus - no question mentions 'Item' or 'section' at all (checked all `question`/`category`/`subtype`/`intent_label` fields). This is a stronger version of the zero-example situation already user-approved at Task 3.8 (narrative/section_summary intents). Unlike Task 3.8, there is no partial subset to score against - the navigation capability itself is mechanical (deterministic lookup over an already-computed structural artifact), so it is implemented and tested against the one ground-truth surface that DOES exist: Task 2.8's own frozen structural-parsing output (`artifacts/primary_docs/parsed/*.json`, 990 documents, canonical Item detection already verified in Task 2.8's own test suite). Formal evaluation in this task measures the navigation layer's own correctness/coverage over that corpus, not natural-language question answering (which stays out of scope, generation_enabled=false, same as every other Phase 3 task).

reused_not_reimplemented.section_boundary_detection: src.parse.primary_html._CANONICAL_ITEMS and its Section-15 last-occurrence-wins heading detector (Task 2.8, frozen, unmodified) - the ONE section-boundary source of truth. This task never re-derives Item boundaries; it only looks up section_id on already-parsed StructuralNode records.
reused_not_reimplemented.parsed_corpus: artifacts/primary_docs/parsed/<doc_key>.json (Task 2.8, locally-derived/gitignored, deterministic given source_sha256 + parser_config_hash) - 990 of the corpus's 1,493 documents have been HTML-parsed; navigation coverage is bounded by this, an honest documented limitation, not a new sampling decision by this task.
reused_not_reimplemented.filing_identity: data/xbrl.duckdb's `submissions` table (cik, adsh, fiscal_year, form) - the same frozen source Task 2.1/2.2's truth contract and Task 2.8's own document_id construction (`primary:{cik}:{accession}`, src.parse.source_identity) are built from.

new_this_task.extract_item_reference(text): text-only regex extraction of a canonical SEC Item id (e.g. '7', '7A') from free text - returns None rather than guessing, mirroring Task 2.8's own section_id=None-over-a-wrong-guess policy. Lives in the new src/nav module, not in Task 3.8's frozen src/router/rules.py.
new_this_task.resolve_filing_document_id(cik, fiscal_y: (cik, fiscal_year) -> document_id via `submissions` filtered to form='10-K'. Outcomes: found (exactly one match), filing_not_found (zero matches), ambiguous_filing (>1 matching 10-K submission for the same cik+fiscal_year, e.g. an amended filing - 43 such groups exist in the corpus; never silently picks one, same policy as Task 3.10's XbrlFactIndex).
new_this_task.navigate_to_section(cik, fiscal_year, it: loads exactly one document's parsed JSON file (never scans the other 989), filters its nodes to section_id == item, and returns only those. Outcomes: found, section_not_found (item not detected in that document), filing_not_parsed (document_id resolved but never HTML-parsed by Task 2.8), filing_not_found, ambiguous_filing.

eval_population.source: every (cik, fiscal_year) pair with a successfully Task-2.8-parsed 10-K (990 documents) crossed with every canonical Item id Task 2.8's own section-heading detector actually found in that document (from the parsed node's own section_id field - real, already-computed ground truth, not new hand labeling).
measures: filing_resolution_rate: fraction of (cik, fiscal_year) pairs for parsed documents that resolve back to the correct document_id via resolve_filing_document_id (round-trip correctness against Task 2.8's own manifest).
section_found_rate: fraction of (document, detected-item) pairs where navigate_to_section returns outcome='found' with the correct section_title.

scope_tightness (hard invariant, must be 100%): every returned node's section_id equals exactly the requested item (zero cross-section leakage), and node_count is always strictly less than total_document_node_count (proof no global/full-document retrieval occurred).

phase3_12_config.extraction_source: cik/fiscal_year are extracted from question TEXT ONLY via Task 3.8's frozen, unmodified CompanyGazetteer/extract_fiscal_years - never a question record's own hidden ground-truth fields. Not applicable to the corpus-level structural eval above, which uses each parsed document's own known (cik, fiscal_year) identity directly (there is no DEV question text to leak from for this eval population).

limitations: PROJECT_EXECUTION.md's Task 3.12 example query ('Summarize Item 7 of this filing') has zero matching examples anywhere in the 1,932-question DEV corpus; formal evaluation here measures the navigation layer's own structural correctness/coverage against Task 2.8's parsed corpus instead of natural-language question answering (generation stays out of scope, same as every other Phase 3 task).

Navigation coverage is bounded by Task 2.8's own HTML-parsing coverage: only 990 of the corpus's 1493 documents have been parsed - an honest, pre-existing gap, not a new sampling decision by this task.
Skipped 2 parsed documents with no matching submissions row and 0 with a non-10-K form.
No retrieval, embedding call, reranking, CRAG gating, or generation in this path - a pure structural lookup over Task 2.8's already-computed section boundaries.
next_task_readiness: filing_resolution_rate=0.9990, section_found_rate=0.9988, scope_leak_rate=0.0000 (must be 0.0 - hard safety invariant).
